thread:
tara: FYI hitting a weird pattern on onboarding sample app — users see duplicate completions after 429 + token refresh. repro steps short: call -> 429 -> refresh -> retry -> duplicate downstream webhook firing.
sam: ugh. can you paste logs? is the SDK sending the original request twice or is server replaying?
tara: logs look like SDK resend. snippet: `POST /v1/generate` -> 429 response -> client does `auth.refresh()` -> client retries same body. But webhook got two distinct completions (different IDs) about ~200ms apart.
kevin: do we have idempotency keys wired in onboarding sampleapp? I thought we relied on safe-replay window + idempotency header in node/python SDKs.
tara: onboarding sampleapp currently only sets an `Idempotency-Key` for create-payment style flows, not for generation requests. assumption was safe-replay heuristics would prevent dupes.
sam: hmm, generation has side-effects because we post results to customers. Two approaches: (1) teach sampleapp to set idempotency-key per request (cheap), or (2) make SDK backoff/replay behavior stricter on 429 during token rotation so we avoid blind immediate retry.
kevin: I wonder if token refresh flow uses a new auth token and then replays without jitter. If multiple clients refresh concurrently you can get thundering rehearsing of the same request. Could add random jitter and a small backoff before immediate retry after refresh.
tara: repro timeline: request->429, SDK starts refresh (200ms), refresh success (120ms), immediate retry -> success. So both original and retried request reached server within 300ms window. Server accepted both and produced separate completions.
sam: can we detect "in-flight after refresh" and dedupe at SDK level by inserting a transient local cache of recent request hashes for e.g., 1s? That would avoid dupes without requiring user-set idempotency-keys.
kevin: possible but brittle. Better to document recommended pattern: set `Idempotency-Key` for any request that triggers downstream side-effects in sampleapp. Meanwhile we should tighten default SDK behavior: add 50-200ms jitter before retry after auth refresh and classify 429 from auth failures separately.
tara: agreed on doc + short-term SDK patch. I'll open a tiny PR to sampleapp to set idempotency for the webhook flow.
sam: I'll file an SDK issue for: (a) jitter on post-refresh retries, (b) optional transient request-hash dedupe toggle, (c) improved logging to show "retry-after-auth-refresh" events.
kevin: also add a note in devex onboarding checklist: "ensure idempotency keys or server-side dedupe for any webhook side-effects; SDKs won’t silently dedupe generation requests".
tara: thanks. small follow-ups: what default jitter window? 50-250ms? and should it be configurable?
sam: make it 100±75ms by default and expose config param `retryPostAuthJitterMs` with max 500ms. Keep off for streaming responses where resume is needed.
kevin: +1. tara pls include a minimal repro script in the PR so SRE can run a quick check.
devtools-bot: created issue #4021: "sdk: jitter retries after auth refresh to reduce duplicate successes (generation)"
tara: perfect. I'll do PR for sampleapp + repro and link to #4021. thanks all :thumbsup:
